title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with funding rounds and strategic partnerships as companies and governments alike gear up for an increasingly crowded orbital environment. Meanwhile, the specter of military operations in space looms larger, with implications for both commercial and defense sectors.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy Continues
themes.body: Tomorrow.io's recent $35 million funding boost highlights the ongoing investment trend in space tech, while True Anomaly's $190 million Series C round underscores the appetite for innovative solutions. As the space economy expands, expect more players to vie for a slice of the financial pie.

themes.title: Military Operations in Space
themes.body: The narrative that the next war will be fought in orbit is gaining traction, with the Pentagon emphasizing the importance of space resilience. Partnerships like Anduril and L3Harris's tactical SDA constellation bid reflect a shift towards integrating commercial capabilities into defense strategies.

themes.title: Launch Infrastructure Challenges
themes.body: A recent CSF report warns of potential bottlenecks with the projected surge of over 7,000 satellites by the mid-2030s, raising questions about the US's launch infrastructure readiness. As demand escalates, the industry must address these logistical hurdles or risk falling behind.

themes.title: Emerging Defense-Tech Landscape
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window appears to be cracking open, with a noticeable uptick in interest from venture capitalists. This shift is further evidenced by the rise of AI-focused defense startups, indicating a blend of traditional defense with cutting-edge technology.
